protocol.name: aqueous_shell_v1

description.summary: Aqueous shell state and typed policy operations

protocol.description: Privileged same-session shell interface. JSON schema 1 is documented in aqueous-shell-v1.md. IDs are opaque strings scoped to the session token. State is committed policy state, not animation frame geometry. Clients acknowledge each bounded batch before another is sent. Intermediate states may be coalesced; base_sequence identifies the state to which a delta applies.

entry.name: above
entry.summary: rendered above the window content (titlebar layer)

entry.name: below
entry.summary: rendered below the window content (shadow/backdrop layer)

entry.name: session_reload
entry.summary: reload configuration through the normal policy reload path

request.name: subscribe

description.summary: request an initial snapshot and subsequent changes

request.description: May be sent once. The server sends at most one unacknowledged batch.

request.name: command
request.description: One outstanding command per object. Empty strings select documented defaults. Targets are opaque window/workspace/group IDs; output values are connector names. State values are true/false. Strings are bounded to 1024 bytes. Failures are recoverable result events. Window and session mutations are unavailable while locked or under external or comparison policy.

event.name: data
event.description: Concatenate fragments until done. At most 4 MiB per complete batch. A fragment may split a UTF-8 codepoint; parse only the complete batch.

request.name: subscribe_unmanaged
request.description: Like subscribe, additionally includes unmanaged_window entities. Exactly one of subscribe or subscribe_unmanaged may be used per manager. These IDs cannot be used with managed window commands.

request.name: get_window_decoration

description.summary: create a shell-drawn decoration surface for a window

request.description:
Create an aqueous_shell_decoration_v1 decoration surface attached to the managed window identified by window_id, a shell window ID from the state stream. The decoration is placed above or below the window content per placement and follows the window through moves, resizes, workspace transitions and hiding. The shell client draws the decoration content and owns its theming; the compositor keeps window policy. While a mapped above-placement decoration exists the compositor suppresses its own borders for that window.
The result event reports request_id with a recoverable status. On any non-applied status the created object is inert and must be destroyed by the client. Only available under integrated policy and an unlocked session; Wayland-bound manager objects only.

request.name: window_interactive_move

description.summary: start an interactive pointer move of a window

request.description: Start an interactive move for the window identified by window_id, typically in response to a pointer button press on a shell decoration surface. serial must be the serial of the button press which triggered the request; invalid serials are rejected with invalid status. seat selects the seat by name; empty selects the sole seat. The result event reports request_id.

request.name: window_interactive_resize

description.summary: start an interactive pointer resize of a window

request.description: Like window_interactive_move, but starts an interactive resize. edges is a bitmask of xdg_toplevel resize edge values (top 1, bottom 2, left 4, right 8) and must not be zero. The result event reports request_id.

interface.name: aqueous_shell_decoration_v1
interface.description:
A decoration surface created through aqueous_shell_manager_v1.get_window_decoration. Rendering order matches aqueous_decoration_v1: below-placement decorations render under the window content, above-placement decorations over it. The decoration follows its window through moves, resizes, workspace transitions and hiding; the shell client owns its content and theming.
Unlike aqueous_decoration_v1 there is no external window manager render sequence: requests may be sent at any time and the compositor applies them in its next rendering transaction.

entry.name: no_commit
entry.summary: failed to commit the surface before the compositor render

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the decoration object and that it may be safely destroyed.

request.name: set_offset

description.summary: set offset from the window's top left corner

request.description: This request sets the offset of the decoration surface from the top left corner of the window, in logical pixels. If never sent, the offset is (0, 0).

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x relative to top left window corner

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y relative to top left window corner

request.name: sync_next_commit

description.summary: sync next commit with the compositor render

request.description: Synchronize application of the next wl_surface.commit request on the decoration surface with the compositor's next rendering transaction, so decoration updates land atomically with window moves and workspace transitions. The client must commit the decoration surface after this request and before the compositor's next render finishes; failure to do so is a protocol error.
